findings.description: The client uses recvfrom with NULL address and accepts datagrams from anyone.
With fixed-size buffers, UDP datagrams that exceed the buffer are silently truncated by recvfrom.
recvfrom blocks forever if the server is down or network is disrupted.
User input is sent in plaintext over UDP.
Hardcoding an IP/port reduces flexibility and can be brittle.
Sending strlen(buffer) + 1 sends the terminating NUL byte over the network unnecessarily.
